chunks: And from him (Al-Hilli) from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah from Ja'far from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he was asked:

About a man who prayed without ablution, or forgot a prayer that he did not perform, or slept through it, so he said: 'He must make it up whenever he remembers it, whether in the night or day. When the time for the current prayer enters and he has not completed what has passed, he should make up the prayer whose time has not yet passed, as it is more deserving, so let him make it up. When he has made it up, let him pray what has passed from what is gone, and he should not offer a voluntary rak'ah until he has completed all the obligatory prayer.'
ai.seo_question: How should a Muslim make up for missed prayers if they slept through them or forgot them?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a precise hierarchy for compensating missed obligatory prayers (qada), prioritizing the oldest missed prayer over the current one to ensure the fulfillment of divine obligations without delay. The ruling further clarifies that voluntary prayers (nafl) are suspended until all missed fard prayers are completed, reflecting the scholarly principle of giving precedence to the debt owed to God over supererogatory acts. This guidance underscores the importance of timely rectification of worship errors in Shia jurisprudence.
